name: Endurance training (running and other steady aerobic exercise)
origin: People have run long distances for thousands of years, jogging for health became a mass movement in the 1960s and 1970s, and in 1979 psychiatrist John Greist and colleagues at the University of Wisconsin published one of the first trials of running as a treatment for depression.
summary: Endurance training means moving continuously at a steady effort you can keep up for a long time, such as running, jogging, cycling, swimming or rowing for 20 minutes or more. Running is the example here, and steady aerobic exercise like it is the most studied kind of exercise for depression. Unlike the bursts and rests of HIIT or the lifting of strength training, its defining feature is an even rhythm kept up over time.
theoryOfChange: Regular aerobic exercise builds heart and lung fitness and tends to improve sleep, and it is thought to lift mood through brain changes such as more of the growth factor BDNF. Single runs can also bring a short-term lift: in a 2021 placebo-controlled trial with 63 people, 45 minutes of running, compared with walking, raised euphoria, eased anxiety and increased the body's own cannabis-like chemicals (endocannabinoids), and blocking opioids did not stop these effects, which challenges the old idea that endorphins cause the runner's high. A running habit also adds routine, a sense of progress and, in groups, company, which may help too.
whatYouDo: You move at a steady pace you can hold, usually still able to speak in short sentences, for about 20 to 60 minutes, and beginners often start with walk-run intervals and build up over weeks. People run alone, with a friend or in a club, outdoors or on a treadmill, and cycling, swimming and rowing work the same way. In the 2023 Dutch MOTAR study, running therapy meant group runs at least twice a week for 16 weeks.
typicalDose: The WHO 2020 guidelines advise adults to get 150 to 300 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity (about 5 or 6 out of 10 for effort) or 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous activity (7 or 8 out of 10), or a mix, for example 30 minutes on 5 days at a moderate pace or 25 minutes on 3 days at a vigorous one. Depression trials have run for weeks to months (16 weeks in MOTAR), and the 2024 network meta-analysis found weak evidence that 10-week programs work at least as well as longer ones; the habit itself is meant to continue.
keyTechniques: Gradual increases in time or distance
Easy days and rest days between harder sessions
Group or club runs for company and routine
Cross-training with cycling, swimming or rowing

evidence.summary: Steady aerobic exercise is the most studied exercise for depression, and many meta-analyses find that it reduces symptoms. A 2024 BMJ network meta-analysis (Noetel and colleagues, 218 trials, 14,170 people with major depression) found that walking or jogging gave moderate reductions compared with active control conditions (effect size 0.62), among the largest of any exercise type, with bigger effects at higher intensity, but only one trial had a low risk of bias, so confidence was rated low. In the 2023 Dutch MOTAR study of 141 patients with depression or anxiety disorders, 16 weeks of group running led to remission about as often as antidepressants (43% versus 45%) and improved physical health more (weight, waist size, blood pressure and heart rate), but only a minority agreed to be randomized, so most patients chose their own treatment.

goodFitFor: People with low mood, stress or anxiety who like rhythm, routine and measurable progress, and want a low-cost practice they can do alone or with others. It can also suit people with depression who want a non-drug option alongside other care, chosen together with their clinician.
cautions: Injuries are common: across studies about 4 in 10 runners got injured during follow-up, most often around the knee, ankle and lower leg, so build up time and distance gradually and include rest. Training hard without enough recovery can lead to lasting fatigue, falling performance and low mood (overreaching, and in severe cases overtraining syndrome), and for a minority exercise becomes compulsive, which deserves professional attention, especially alongside disordered eating. People with heart disease or other medical conditions should get advice first, and no one should stop antidepressants without talking to their doctor.
namingNote: The request listed this point as endurance sport, for example running. It covers any steady, continuous aerobic exercise (running, cycling, swimming, rowing), with running as the example and the source of most of the research cited here. Interval cardio is the HIIT point and leisurely walking in nature is the nature point, although some cited trials group walking and jogging together.
